architecture.approach: The tenancy half of the schema is already shipped and migrated, so this plan adds the clinical half in one additive migration, keeps the in-memory test double in step, and produces the demo dataset. Patient, Doctor and Appointment land together because they reference each other; splitting them would mean three migrations with no value. The migration is pure DDL - CREATE TABLE, CREATE INDEX, foreign keys - with no DROP, no TRUNCATE and no rewrite of an existing table, which is what makes the additive guarantee provable on a populated database. The test double is part of the change rather than cleanup: adding models to schema.prisma without teaching memory-prisma leaves the API suite unable to construct a patient or appointment. The seed is deterministic and idempotent with no new dependency - a small seeded PRNG plus upserts on natural keys.

dataModel.flowDescription: prisma migrate deploy creates the three clinical tables and their indexes on top of the existing tenancy schema; the seed then upserts 3 clinics, 10 doctors, 200 patients and 600 appointments through Prisma; BP-015 to BP-019 query those rows. No existing table or row is altered by the migration.

securityConsiderations.description: Every clinical table carries clinicId with a foreign key to Clinic, so tenant scoping is a schema guarantee: a query that omits the tenant filter cannot silently join across clinics. The migration is static DDL with no user input and no raw SQL is introduced; all access goes through Prisma's parameterised client (CON-516).

The seed reads DATABASE_URL from the environment only and refuses to run when NODE_ENV=production, so a development fixture cannot be written to a deployed database (CON-519). Every seeded person is fictional - fixed name list, @riaya.local and example.org addresses - and the file header restates CON-506.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: The migration is small DDL on three new tables plus two indexes, so migrate deploy on an empty database takes a few hundred milliseconds; the 60-second budget covers CI cold starts rather than the work itself.
The seed writes 813 rows in sequential upserts inside one transaction, which stays well inside the 60-second budget and leaves no partial state if it fails.
Additive-only DDL means no table rewrite and no long lock on existing tables, so the migration applies to a populated database without a backfill window.

risks.description: The generated migration contains an unexpected destructive statement.
risks.mitigation: T1.2 reads the emitted SQL before it is committed; DROP or TRUNCATE is a stop condition, not a review note.

risks.description: The in-memory test double drifts from schema.prisma and tests pass against a fiction.
risks.mitigation: T1.4 adds the same three models to the double in the same change.

risks.description: The seed doubles rows on a second run and inflates the demo dataset.
risks.mitigation: Upsert on a natural key per entity; T3.2 runs the seed twice and compares counts.

risks.description: The seed runs against a non-development database.
risks.mitigation: The NODE_ENV guard in T2.2 refuses rather than warns.

risks.description: endsAt > startsAt cannot be expressed in Prisma, so invalid rows become possible later.
risks.mitigation: EC-003 records the gap and names BP-019 as the owner instead of implying the schema covers it.
